models.summary: You can use it for summaries, database queries and high-volume jobs, at around 75% less cost than Haiku 4.5.

extra.source_text: Introducing Claude Haiku 5.5: the cheapest, fastest, and most capable small model we’ve ever released. Claude Haiku 5.5 is designed for high-volume, cost-sensitive tasks. It reliably handles quick and repetitive workloads (like summaries, compactions, database queries, and classification requests). It pairs well with Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 as a subagent on coding work. And, since it’s also our fastest model to date, it works especially well for speed-sensitive tasks like live customer support and browser use.¹ Haiku 5.5 is available at a much lower price than Haiku 4.5. On average, it now costs around 75% less to run.² Along with this launch, we’re making improvements to the value of our model range. We’re halving the price of Claude Sonnet 5.5’s cache reads, which means Sonnet 5.5 now runs around 20% cheaper on most agentic work. And we’re introducing a new monthly API credit for our Claude Max and Team subscribers, designed to support our users in building new agents and applications that run on the Claude Platform. Compared with the model we use today, we saw over a 30% reduction in latency for task completions and up to 2.5x faster inference per agent turn. With widespread usage comes the need to manage efficiency and cost, and to find the best model to suit the task at hand. In early testing, Claude Haiku 5.5 scored 11 points higher than Haiku 4.5 at about half the latency. We’d put it to use on analytical work that runs at scale, from cost reports to financial summaries and weekly recurring reviews.” Company Box Author Yashodha Bhavnani, VP of AI Products Quote “The short and high-volume work is where Claude Haiku 5.5 fits for us, like quick lookups, subagents, and summaries. While a bigger model builds the deck, a Haiku 5.5 subagent goes into the 10-K and pulls the segment revenue line the deck needs. It’s accurate enough that we’d trust it there, and fast and cheap enough that we can run it a lot.” Company Rogo Author Alex Wang, Applied AI Quote “Claude Haiku 5.5 joins the sidekick lineup in Devin Fusion as an excellent option. With Haiku 5.5 as the sidekick, Fusion holds a top-tier FrontierCode score of 66.2 while cutting cost and latency. You can try it today in the Devin CLI with Opus 5.5 as the lead.” Company Cognition Author Walden Yan, Co-Founder & CPO Pricing The table below shows how Claude Haiku 5.5’s pricing compares to our other models. Haiku 5.5 is especially good value when used for tasks with prompts up to 100,000 tokens, which make up around 90% of requests to our previous Haiku model. Price per 1 million tokens Haiku 5.5 prompts up to / over 100k Haiku 4.5 Sonnet 5.5 Cache reads $0.01 / $0.05 $0.10 $0.10 Cache writes $0.125 / $0.625 $1.25 $2.50 Input tokens $0.10 / $0.50 $1.00 $2.00 Output tokens $0.50 / $2.50 $5.00 $10.00 Safety Alignment. Claude Haiku 5.5 shows major improvements across almost all of our alignment evaluations relative to Haiku 4.5. In particular, we found far fewer instances of misaligned behavior, and a lower willingness to cooperate with misuse. The model’s system card describes our evaluation process and results in more detail. Safeguards. Consistent with its capabilities, Haiku 5.5’s cybersecurity safeguards are more restrictive than Haiku 4.5’s, but somewhat less restrictive than those we’ve applied to other recent models. In cybersecurity, they permit a wider range of defensive tasks than our safeguards for Sonnet 5.5, but they still block penetration testing and other techniques more likely to be used by attackers. Haiku 5.5’s biology safeguards are the same as for Sonnet 5, Sonnet 5.5, and Opus 5. They allow research biology questions but restrict access to requests that we judge as likely to cause harm. Organizations working on wider-ranging biology and cyber activities can apply to our Life Sciences Verification Program and Cyber Verification Program . Availability Claude Haiku 5.5 is available now on all platforms, including Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure. On the Claude Platform, developers can get started with claude-haiku-5-5 . See our migration guide for details. Further updates Alongside our new pricing for Claude Haiku 5.5, we’re making further improvements to the value of our models and products. First, starting today, we’re lowering the price of cache reads on Claude Sonnet 5.5 . Cache reads now cost 50% less: $0.10 per million tokens rather than $0.20. Because cache reads make up a large share of models’ token consumption, this reduces the cost of Sonnet 5.5 on most agentic tasks by around 20%. For instance, here’s what the price cut means for Sonnet 5.5’s performance relative to cost on Terminal-Bench 4.0: Terminal-Bench 4.0 Accuracy vs. cost Haiku 5.5 Haiku 4.5 Sonnet 5.5 ($0.10 cache reads) Sonnet 5.5 ($0.20 cache reads) 0 10 20 30 40 50 60 70 Score (pass@1, %) 0.50 1 2 5 10 Cost per attempt (USD, log scale) Low Med High Xhigh Max Terminal-Bench 4.0 measures how well a model can complete complex, multi-step professional tasks within a command-line interface. This chart illustrates an important difference between Haiku 5.5 and our larger models. Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5 remain better choices for complex agentic coding tasks like those measured by Terminal-Bench 4.0. By contrast, Haiku 5.5 is best suited to more narrowly scoped tasks that might otherwise have been cost-prohibitive with previous versions of Claude—like compaction, summarization, or subagent work. Second, this week, we’ll roll out a new monthly API credit to all Max and Team subscribers for use on the Claude Platform . Max 5x users will get $100 in credits per month, Max 20x users will get $200, and Team subscribers will receive up to $500, pooled across their users. These credits are designed to allow our users to experiment with building tools, apps, and agents that call our API. They can be used on any of our models. For more information, see our Help Center article . For developers, we’re also updating our Claude Python and TypeScript SDKs to add support for computer use and browser use in beta. Haiku 5.5 is especially well-suited to these tasks, given its combination of speed, capability, and price. You can read more about this in our Claude Platform docs . Footnotes 1 Claude Haiku 5.5 is our fastest model to date at each model’s standard speed, although it runs less quickly than our Opus models in Fast Mode. 2 Claude Haiku 5.5 is priced 90% lower than Claude Haiku 4.5 for requests up to 100,000 tokens, and 50% lower for requests over 100,000 tokens. On Haiku 4.5, 90% of requests fell into the former category. This calculation also accounts for changes between Haiku 4.5 and Haiku 5.5 in how many tokens are used to complete a given piece of work: Haiku 5.5 has an updated tokenizer (similar to Sonnet 5.5’s and Opus 5.5’s), which means it uses slightly more tokens per task.

tools.headline: Talorys: a free personal AI assistant that runs in your own Cloudflare account
tools.summary: You can use it to chat, keep notes and tasks, and set reminders, with data stored in your own Cloudflare account.
tools.why_it_matters: If you want a private helper for tasks and reminders, your data stays in your own Cloudflare account and it is designed to fit the free plan.
tools.for_builders: Run npx create-talorys@latest in your terminal, then follow the prompts to log in to Cloudflare and set an owner password.

extra.candidate_title: Talorys – A self-hosted personal AI agent on Cloudflare's free tier
extra.source_text: Talorys Your personal AI agent. Your own cloud. Talorys is a free, open-source personal AI assistant that runs entirely inside your own Cloudflare account . It chats with you, remembers what matters, manages tasks, notes and projects, and runs reminders and routines on a schedule — without any server, database or account operated by the Talorys developers. One person. One Cloudflare account. One command. One personal AI agent. npx create-talorys@latest 1. What Talorys is A private assistant — chat with streaming responses, Markdown and tool activity indicators. Memory — durable personal facts and preferences you can view, edit and delete. Only the most relevant memories are sent to the model on each turn. Semantic recall (optional) — finds memories by meaning as well as keyword, and lists them newest first with their saved date. Off by default; turn it on with the Semantic memory recall switch near the bottom of Settings → AI (its other settings appear once it is on), or install with --semantic . See docs/semantic-recall.md . Memory history — facts that change over time: when you say you sold your car, the old one is kept as a past fact instead of being treated as current, and unclear conflicts wait for your review. See docs/memory-history.md . Tasks, notes and projects — full CRUD in the UI, and from chat ("Add a task to review my project tomorrow"). Automations — one-time and recurring reminders, daily task digests and optional AI routines, delivered to an in-app notification center. They run on Durable Object alarms, so nothing has to stay online. Single-user by design — no signup, no accounts, no teams. The installer sets the owner password. Works without AI — tasks, notes, memories and reminders keep working if Workers AI is unavailable or your free quota is used up. Screenshots Chat with tool activity Tasks Memory (dark mode) Automations 2. How it works Browser ──HTTPS──▶ Cloudflare Pages (React app + /api Pages Function) │ service binding (no public URL) ▼ Private Worker (Hono router) │ getAgentByName("personal-agent") ▼ TalorysAgent — Cloudflare Agents SDK Durable Object ├─ SQLite: conversations, memories, tasks, notes, projects, │ automations, sessions, settings, usage ├─ Workers AI: @cf/zai-org/glm-4.7-flash (streaming + tool calling) └─ Alarms: reminders and recurring schedules The browser only ever talks to your *.pages.dev site. /api/* requests run a Pages Function that forwards them over a service binding to the agent Worker. The agent Worker is deployed with workers_dev: false and preview_urls: false : it has no public URL . Authentication and authorization happen in the Worker, not the frontend. Chat responses stream as Server-Sent Events end-to-end. More detail: docs/architecture.md . 3. Cloudflare services used Service Used for Free plan Cloudflare Pages Frontend + Pages Function Yes Cloudflare Workers Private API Worker Yes Durable Objects (SQLite) All data, scheduling alarms Yes Workers AI Chat model ( @cf/zai-org/glm-4.7-flash ) Yes, daily allocation Talorys does not provision R2, D1, KV, Vectorize, AI Search, Workflows or any paid service. 4. Deploy npx create-talorys@latest The installer: Checks Node.js (22+) and uses its bundled Wrangler CLI (any globally installed wrangler / cf is detected but not required). Verifies your Cloudflare login, or opens Cloudflare's authorization page in your browser . Lets you choose an account (if you have several) and an agent name. Asks for an owner password (hidden input, strength-checked). It is hashed locally with PBKDF2-SHA256 and stored only as a Cloudflare secret. Generates a 256-bit session secret and unique resource names ( talorys-<id>-agent , talorys-<id>-web ). Deploys the private Worker (creating its SQLite Durable Object), stores secrets, creates and deploys the Pages project with the service binding. Verifies the live deployment (frontend, auth endpoint, unauthenticated rejection, storage health) without running any AI inference. Prints the real https://….pages.dev URL reported by Cloudflare. It writes a talorys/ directory containing talorys.json (installation id, account id, resource names, URL — no secrets ) and the deployable artifacts. Keep it for updates. Interrupted? Run the same command again in the same place. It reconciles what already exists: no duplicate resources, no password re-prompt if the password is already configured, and no data is ever deleted . Non-interactive installs: TALORYS_OWNER_PASSWORD=... npx create-talorys@latest --yes --account-id <id> (with CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN set if you are not logged in). Permissions Browser login uses Wrangler's standard OAuth flow — no Global API Key. If you use an API token instead, it needs: Account › Workers Scripts › Edit Account › Cloudflare Pages › Edit Account › Workers AI › Read Account › Account Settings › Read User › User Details › Read (optional; shows your email) See docs/deployment.md . 5. Access Open the URL the installer prints, enter your owner password, and start chatting. Sign in from any number of devices — they are all the same owner. Manage sessions under Settings → Security . Forgot the password? From your talorys/ directory: npx create-talorys@latest reset-password This replaces the password secret and signs out every device. 6. Where your data lives All data is stored in a single SQLite-backed Durable Object ( personal-agent ) in your Cloudflare account . Talorys has no telemetry, analytics, tracking or advertising code and sends nothing to its developers. Cloudflare processes your data to provide its services — including running Workers AI inference on your chat messages and the relevant memories included in each prompt. Review Cloudflare's privacy policy and Workers AI terms. Security model and threat mitigations: docs/security.md . 7. What is free and what may cost money Talorys is designed to fit the Cloudflare Workers Free plan and never enables paid features on its own. It is not "unlimited free", though: Free plans have account-level quotas (requests, Durable Object usage, a daily Workers AI Neuron allocation). Quotas are set by Cloudflare and can change. When the AI allocation is exhausted, chat shows a clear message and resumes after the daily reset. Everything else keeps working, and your data is untouched. If your account is on a paid plan, usage beyond included amounts is billed by Cloudflare under your plan. Built-in guardrails (adjustable in Settings → AI ): max output tokens, max context tokens (older history is summarized), max tool calls and reasoning steps per request, max AI requests per day (every model call counts, including each reasoning step and history summary), and max scheduled AI runs per day. Simple reminders and task digests never use AI. The Usage panel shows local estimates and links to the Cloudflare dashboard for exact Neuron usage. 8. Local development Requirements: Node.js 22+. git clone https://github.com/rociiu/talorys.git cd talorys npm install npm run dev npm run dev starts the agent Worker ( wrangler dev , port 8787), the Pages Function proxy with its service binding ( wrangler pages dev , port 8788) and the Vite UI ( http://localhost:5173 ) in one terminal. It creates apps/agent/.dev.vars with a local password ( talorys-dev-password , override with TALORYS_DEV_PASSWORD ) and uses the deterministic mock AI provider, so no Cloudflare login is needed. State persists in .wrangler/state . Other scripts: npm run build , npm test , npm run test:e2e , npm run test:pack , npm run typecheck , npm run lint . See docs/development.md . 9. Back up your data Settings → Privacy → Download backup produces talorys-backup.json with conversations, memories, tasks, notes, projects, settings and automations (never sessions or credentials). Import validates the file and merges it in one transaction; importing the same backup twice is harmless, and a memory you edited locally after the backup was made is not overwritten. Memory history (current vs. past facts) is included. Older backups import as before. Settings include the effective installer defaults. If an imported timezone changes, retained local automations are also rescheduled in that timezone. A backup file is treated as untrusted: new automations arrive paused, existing automations are never changed except to pause them, and the model, limits, demo mode, auto-memory and memory history settings are kept as they are (the import result lists any it skipped). 10. Update From your talorys/ directory: npx create-talorys@latest update This redeploys the latest Worker and frontend to the same resources. The Durable Object namespace is never recreated (migrations are append-only), the owner password and sessions are kept, and schema migrations run automatically and transactionally on first request. Also available: status and doctor . 11. Troubleshooting Problem Fix Installer stopped midway Re-run the same command; it resumes. "did not pass its health checks yet" New pages.dev sites can take a few minutes. Re-run. Permission errors Use an account where you can edit Workers and Pages, or a token with the permissions above. Chat says the AI allocation is used up Wait for the daily reset; or enable Demo mode in Settings → AI. Locked out after failed logins Wait 15 minutes, or reset the password with the CLI. npx create-talorys@latest doctor checks everything automatically. More in docs/troubleshooting.md . Repository layout apps/agent Private Worker: Hono API, TalorysAgent, tools, SQLite repositories apps/web React + Vite app, Pages Function (functions/api/[[path]].ts) packages/shared Zod schemas, types, recurrence/DST logic, password hashing packages/create-talorys The one-command installer (npm package) tests/e2e Playwright UI tests tests/smoke Optional real-account deployment test docs/ Architecture, deployment, development, security, troubleshooting Credits Thanks to everyone who has contributed to Talorys: Roc Yu (@rociiu) — creator and maintainer Derek (@KrunchMuffin) — Node.js 22 requirement, task deletion and cancelled-turn fixes, Windows build support Rudy Celekli (@rudycelekli) — automation lifecycle, deployment verification, and portable backup settings fixes Andrew B (@who) — opt-in semantic recall for memories Mendy Landa (@MendyLanda) — single-Worker deployment Michael Tuszynski (@michaeltuszynski) — untrusted backup import handling and daily AI budget accounting License MIT

extra.candidate_title: GPT-6 and Intelligent UI for everyone
extra.source_text: October 7, 2026 Product Release GPT‑6 and Intelligent UI for everyone Loading… Share Last month we introduced the first GPT‑6 models for paid customers and today we're bringing that next generation of intelligence to more people with a new GPT‑6 model built for more than 1.2 billion people who use ChatGPT each week. GPT‑6 in ChatGPT introduces Intelligent UI, a new capability that allows ChatGPT to answer quickly with fully interactive user interfaces that make everyday answers more visual, make learning complex topics easier and that can quickly create a tool to solve a task right in the moment. break down the design of a 7‑speed bike All Frame Wheels Drivetrain Brakes Cockpit 7‑Speed Bicycle 7‑Speed Bicycle 7‑Speed Bicycle Chat Images Intelligent UI A 7‑speed bicycle brings together a frame, handlebars, wheels and hand-operated brakes. Seven gears let the rider adjust pedaling effort as the drivetrain turns effort into motion. Upright bars guide the steering, gears vary the effort, and hand brakes control the pace. Five connected systems The frame carries the rider; the drivetrain turns effort into motion. Select a system to explore its role. A strong foundation Two triangles connect the saddle, steering and pedals. The fork holds the front wheel and turns with the bars. Made to keep rolling Spokes connect each hub to its rim and support the rider. The tires surround the rims and grip the ground. Seven ways to move The pedals turn the chain, driving the rear wheel. Seven gears let the rider adjust pedaling effort for climbs, flats and descents. Control at the rim Hand levers pull cables that bring the brake pads against the rims, turning a squeeze into controlled slowing. Steering and support The handlebars and stem steer the front wheel. The saddle and seatpost support the rider and set the sitting position. break down the design of a 7‑speed bike Chat Chat 7‑Speed Bicycle Side view of a 7-speed bicycle with five connected systems All Frame Wheels Drivetrain Brakes Cockpit A 7‑speed bicycle brings together a frame, handlebars, wheels and hand-operated brakes. Seven gears let the rider adjust pedaling effort as the drivetrain turns effort into motion. Introducing Intelligent UI We’ve trained GPT‑6 to compose responses using text, visuals and interactive elements, choosing how they fit together based on your question. With Intelligent UI, responses can include graphics, tappable buttons, forms, charts, and interactive experiences you can use directly in your conversation. The format depends on what you’re asking. A comparison might work best side by side. An explanation might be easier to understand through an interactive diagram. And when a simple text answer is the most useful response, ChatGPT can give you that. More visual responses to everyday questions ChatGPT can make a plan easier to follow by showing how it fits together. The timing for a Sunday roast can sit alongside the recipe, or the stops on a road trip can appear on a map, with notes on what’s worth a detour. Learn complex topics more easily Visual and interactive explanations let you explore how something works, change an input to see what happens, or work through a problem step by step. Create interactive experiences just by asking You can also ask ChatGPT to create a tool for the task at hand, such as a calculator to explore how savings could grow, a bill splitter for dinner with friends, or a game you can play in the conversation. How Intelligent UI works With Intelligent UI, we gave GPT‑6 the freedom to create the most useful interface for each question, while keeping the experience fast and familiar across web and mobile. We built a library of native, streamable components, along with a compiler that processes the interface as the model generates it. The library gives each response a familiar design foundation while leaving the model room to decide how the pieces fit together. The compiler allows the interface to appear progressively as the model generates it, without waiting for the entire response to be complete. We expanded our training methods to help the model make thoughtful decisions about content, layout, visuals, and interaction. This included evaluating the interfaces it creates for clarity, usefulness, and completeness. GPT‑6 learned to use the component library and make good design decisions, including how to organize information clearly, when to use interactivity, and when a simple text response is enough. There's still work ahead to improve the model's design judgment and expand what it can create, but Intelligent UI marks a significant shift in how people interact with ChatGPT. Instead of fitting every question into the same conversational format, ChatGPT can combine UI, data, and actions to create entirely new ways for people to explore, understand, and interact with information. Frontier Intelligence – delivered more quickly With GPT‑6, we’re also making it possible for ChatGPT to begin answering while it continues to think. GPT‑5.6 Instant GPT‑6 Instant With the introduction of reasoning models, users could get help with much harder problems, but had to wait for the model to finish thinking before getting an answer. Now, ChatGPT can interleave thinking with answering. We trained it to take into account the user’s waiting time and progressively compose an answer using its knowledge and findings up to that point. It learned to build answers across multiple partial responses, each adding useful information without unnecessary filler, while keeping the full answer as cohesive and factual as one written all at once. In an internal evaluation of high-value, everyday agentic tasks, GPT‑6 Extra High is able to begin answering in the same amount of time as GPT‑5.6 Medium while achieving a better overall score than GPT‑5.6 Extra High. For questions that need web search, GPT‑6 Instant starts answering 44% sooner, on average, than GPT‑5.6 Instant. GPT‑6 also improves the quality of answers that require web search. It makes better decisions about when to look something up and more reliably finds information that supports its answer. In an internal evaluation of difficult problems, GPT‑6 correctly addressed the key aspect of the user’s question more often than GPT‑5.6. Deploying GPT‑6 safely As we bring more intelligent AI to more people, we work to improve how it recognizes real-world risks, how honestly it responds, and how well it respects the limits that people set. GPT‑6 makes progress in each of these areas, building on several of Astra’s safety advances to better resist attempts to bypass its safety training, follow safeguards, and be clearer about what it can and can’t do relative to GPT‑5.6 Sol. We updated its safety training based on lessons from real-world use to strengthen protections against high-risk misuse involving cyberattacks, biological threats, and violence. In adversarial testing, GPT‑6 showed stronger resistance to attempts to bypass its safety training, particularly attacks that adapt across multiple turns. GPT‑6 is also trained to respond safely in higher-risk scenarios while avoiding unnecessary refusals of harmless requests. This includes using conversation history and relevant context to recognize risks that may not be apparent from a single prompt. We ran alignment evaluations throughout training, assessing honesty and responses to safety restrictions. GPT‑6 is better at recognizing and communicating the limits of its own capabilities, including when it lacks the information or tools needed to answer. More detail on the results and our review is available in the system card ⁠ (opens in a new window) . Availability GPT‑6 with Intelligent UI starts rolling out globally to ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business and Enterprise tiers today in the Chat tab. Starting tomorrow, the rollout expands to Free and Go tiers. Enterprise availability depends on workplace admin settings. extra.source_text:
An agent skill for creating detailed, interactive isometric illustrations of real-world machines and complex systems. Generates polished SVGs with optional WebGL shaders and 3D effects.

Anatomy

A Claude skill that explains an idea by building it as a real, working object.
Also runs in OpenCode and Codex.
Crafted, interactive isometric figures with many small precise parts, in SVG, WebGL and 3D.

   

Quick start · Gallery · What it makes · Install · Usage · Examples · How it works · Limits

examples/raptor-engine, light theme, firing. The engine and stand are SVG; the plume is a WebGL shader in the same isometric camera.

--- Ask Claude for a figure that explains a technical idea, and Anatomy has it invent a physical thing whose working *is* the concept. A cache key that skips work when nothing changed becomes a pin-tumbler lock that only turns when every pin matches. One GPU context serving many canvases becomes a gantry plotter whose single print head visits 16 wells. Then Claude builds that thing out of dozens of small, solid, shaded parts, puts it in a framed card with a title, a hint and a live readout, makes it move calmly under the pointer and the keyboard, and checks its own work by zooming in on every joint. Every number the figure shows comes from the same small model that moves its parts. ## Quick start ```sh npx skills add wheresryan22/anatomy -g -a claude-code ``` Then, in Claude Code: ```text /anatomy explain how a token bucket rate limiter works, interactive ``` For OpenCode or Codex, swap the agent: `-a opencode` or `-a codex`. OpenCode takes the same `/anatomy` command; in Codex, type `$anatomy`. That's it. No API keys and nothing to `npm install`: the kit uses only Node's built-in modules. ## Gallery
raptor-engine: hover to take it apart into 11 assemblies. An audit proves that no pipe passes through anything, at rest, apart and in every frame between. ripple-tank: SVG apparatus over two WebGL layers (lamp light and caustics on the paper, reflections in the water) driven by a dispersion and optics model.
turning-dial: the 3D mode (beta). About 90 parts are re-projected and re-shaded every frame as you drag the dial. dial-indicator: the smallest example, about 300 lines. Hover to slide the carriage; the needle reads each block.
Every screenshot is the light theme of a page in [`examples/`](examples), captured with the skill's own [`scripts/capture.mjs`](scripts/capture.mjs) and [`scripts/drive.mjs`](scripts/drive.mjs). The built pages are committed: open any `.html` in `examples/` to try it. ## What it makes Three kinds of figure. All three share one kit, one camera and one set of craft rules. | Kind | What it is | Example | |---|---|---| | **SVG** | The core. Solid isometric parts with four-tone shading, painted back to front, in a card with a live readout and eased motion. It ships as a standalone HTML page, a lone `.svg` file with its styles embedded, or React/Next.js components. | `dial-indicator`, `desk-computer`, `arcade-cabinet`, `test-rig` | | **SVG + WebGL** | For what lines can't draw: fire, exhaust, water, caustics, lamp light, glow, steam. The shader runs in a canvas between a back and a front SVG, in the figure's own isometric camera, so it sits inside the drawing. The SVG still reads without WebGL. | `raptor-engine`, `ripple-tank` | | **3D** beta | Parts that turn in true 3D: a dial or turntable that spins, fingers that flex, a piece that breaks off and falls. The moving parts are re-projected and re-shaded by the kit's own rules every frame; the rest of the figure stays static art. | `turning-dial` | Each figure is light or dark. Light is the theme the skill designs for first, shaders included. ## Install Anatomy is a standard [Agent Skill](https://agentskills.io): a folder with a `SKILL.md` at its root. This repository is that folder. Pick one way in: | | Command | Installs to | |---|---|---| | **skills CLI**, for you (Claude Code) | `npx skills add wheresryan22/anatomy -g -a claude-code` | `~/.claude/skills/anatomy` | | **skills CLI**, for you (Antigravity) | `npx skills add wheresryan22/anatomy -g -a antigravity` | `~/.gemini/antigravity/skills/anatomy` | | **skills CLI**, for you (OpenCode) | `npx skills add wheresryan22/anatomy -g -a opencode` | `~/.config/opencode/skills/anatomy` | | **skills CLI**, for you (Codex) | `npx skills add wheresryan22/anatomy -g -a codex` | `~/.agents/skills/anatomy` | | **skills CLI**, for one project | `npx skills add wheresryan22/anatomy` | `.claude/skills/anatomy` for Claude Code, `.agents/skills/anatomy` for Antigravity, OpenCode and Codex | | **git**, for you (Claude Code) | `git clone https://github.com/wheresryan22/anatomy.git ~/.claude/skills/anatomy` | `~/.claude/skills/anatomy` | | **git**, for you (Antigravity) | `git clone https://github.com/wheresryan22/anatomy.git ~/.gemini/antigravity/skills/anatomy` | `~/.gemini/antigravity/skills/anatomy` | | **git**, for you (OpenCode) | `git clone https://github.com/wheresryan22/anatomy.git ~/.config/opencode/skills/anatomy` | `~/.config/opencode/skills/anatomy` | | **git**, for you (Codex) | `git clone https://github.com/wheresryan22/anatomy.git ~/.agents/skills/anatomy` | `~/.agents/skills/anatomy` | | **git**, for one project | `git clone https://github.com/wheresryan22/anatomy.git .claude/skills/anatomy` | `.claude/skills/anatomy` (Claude Code and OpenCode) or `.agents/skills/anatomy` (Antigravity, OpenCode and Codex) | | **Download**, no git | see below | any of the folders above |
With the skills CLI
The [`skills`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills) CLI finds the `SKILL.md` at the root of this repository and installs it as `anatomy`. By default it installs into the current project and asks which agents to set up. `-g` installs it for your user, and `-a claude-code` sets up Claude Code only. Use `-a antigravity`, `-a opencode` or `-a codex` for Antigravity, OpenCode or Codex only. The CLI copies the whole repository, examples included (about 10 MB). It needs a recent Node.js: version 1.7.1 of the CLI asks for 22.20 or later.
With git
Clone the repository into one of the skill folders, so that `SKILL.md` ends up at `/anatomy/SKILL.md`. For Claude Code use `~/.claude/skills/anatomy` or `.claude/skills/anatomy`. For Antigravity use `~/.gemini/antigravity/skills/anatomy` or `.agents/skills/anatomy`. For OpenCode use `~/.config/opencode/skills/anatomy` or `.opencode/skills/anatomy`; OpenCode also reads the Claude Code and `.agents` folders. For Codex use `~/.agents/skills/anatomy` or `.agents/skills/anatomy`. For a project install, commit the folder so your team gets it too. To update later, `git pull` inside that folder.
Download, without git
[Download the ZIP](https://github.com/wheresryan22/anatomy/archive/refs/heads/main.zip), unpack it, rename the folder from `anatomy-main` to `anatomy`, and move it into `~/.claude/skills/` (Claude Code), `~/.gemini/antigravity/skills/` (Antigravity), `~/.config/opencode/skills/` (OpenCode) or `~/.agents/skills/` (Codex). Or in one line on macOS or Linux: ```sh mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills/anatomy && curl -L https://github.com/wheresryan22/anatomy/archive/refs/heads/main.tar.gz | tar -xz --strip-components=1 -C ~/.claude/skills/anatomy ``` For Antigravity, OpenCode or Codex, put the same files in `~/.gemini/antigravity/skills/anatomy`, `~/.config/opencode/skills/anatomy` or `~/.agents/skills/anatomy`: ```sh mkdir -p ~/.gemini/antigravity/skills/anatomy && curl -L https://github.com/wheresryan22/anatomy/archive/refs/heads/main.tar.gz | tar -xz --strip-components=1 -C ~/.gemini/antigravity/skills/anatomy ``` ```sh mkdir -p ~/.config/opencode/skills/anatomy && curl -L https://github.com/wheresryan22/anatomy/archive/refs/heads/main.tar.gz | tar -xz --strip-components=1 -C ~/.config/opencode/skills/anatomy ```
Claude Code picks up new skills in a running session. If the `skills` folder itself did not exist when the session started, run `/reload-skills`. Antigravity and OpenCode list it as `/anatomy` in their chat; restart if it does not show. Codex lists it under `/skills` and runs it with `$anatomy`; restart Codex if it does not show.
Codex: if the browser checks are blocked

extra.source_text:
Animated 3D robot heads for React: TV-headed bots with LED faces that show what your agent is doing.

# robot-heads

Animated 3D robot heads for React. Glossy, TV-headed bots with an LED-matrix face that shows what your agent is doing — thinking, searching, listening, speaking and more — in four shapes, with a springy antenna, knob ears and a light on top that changes with the state.

Drawn on a 2D canvas: no WebGL, no runtime dependencies.

**[Playground →](https://robot-heads.fayaz.workers.dev)**

## Install

```bash
npm install robot-heads
```

React 18 or newer is a peer dependency.

## Quick start

```tsx
import { RobotHead } from 'robot-heads';

function Agent({ status }: { status: 'idle' | 'thinking' | 'speaking' }) {
  return <RobotHead state={status} size={160} />;
}
```

## Shapes

One head, four outlines. Every shape carries the same screen, ears, antenna, screws and back panel, and moves the same way.

```tsx
<RobotHead shape="rectangle" />  {/* the classic TV (default) */}
<RobotHead shape="square" />
<RobotHead shape="circle" />     {/* a porthole */}
<RobotHead shape="hexagon" />    {/* a nut, flat on top */}
```

The list is exported as `robotHeadShapes`.

## States

Each state has its own face on the screen, its own motion and its own antenna light. Switching states plays a short glitch and cross-fade, and the head eases into its new pose.

| State | Screen | Motion |
|---|---|---|
| `idle` | block eyes that blink and glance | looks around, hops now and then |
| `thinking` | heavy-lidded eyes looking up, three pulsing dots | head tilted up, switching sides; amber light pulses |
| `searching` | darting eyes, a beam sweeping the whole screen | head sweeps side to side; cyan beacon |
| `listening` | alert eyes over a live equaliser | head cocked, small nods; steady green light |
| `speaking` | a mouth that moves with the words | bobs as it talks |
| `working` | focused eyes looking down, a progress bar | busy bobbing, a hop with a spin now and then |
| `happy` | `^ ^` eyes and a smile | bouncy hops |
| `error` | red `X X` eyes | shakes its head; red light blinks |
| `sleeping` | closed eyes and rising z's | head drooped, slow breathing; light off |

The list is exported as `robotHeadStates`.

## Props

```tsx
<RobotHead
  shape="rectangle"       // rectangle, square, circle or hexagon
  state="idle"            // what it is doing (above)
  size={160}              // px, the box the robot rests in (below)
  color="#2b49a3"         // the shell
  trimColor="#93a6c8"     // the ears and the antenna's collar
  screenColor="#e8f2ff"   // the LEDs
  speed={1}               // multiplier on every animation
  paused={false}          // hold the state's still pose
  interactive             // follow the pointer, hop and spin on a click
  antenna                 // the antenna's stem and light; off, the knob stays
  floorShadow             // the soft shadow under the head
  seed={0.3}              // 0–1, desyncs blinks and glances in a row of heads
/>
```

Any other attribute (`className`, `style`, `onClick`, `aria-label`, …) goes on the element, and a `ref` reaches the `<canvas>` inside it.

## Sizing and layout

`size` is the robot itself: the element is a `size` × `size` box with the robot at rest centred in it, filling it, antenna included. It lines up with text, sits in a flex row, and centres like an icon or an avatar would.

Its motion is not part of that box. Hops, the antenna's glow and the floor's shadow draw past its edges — like a CSS `box-shadow`, they overflow without taking any room in your layout, and only the box takes clicks. So margins, flex and grid treat it as exactly `size` × `size`; the one thing to watch is a parent with `overflow: hidden` right round it, which would cut off a hop.

## Behaviour

- **Pointer play.** With `interactive` on (the default), the head and eyes follow a nearby pointer, and a click makes it hop with a full spin and a happy face.
- **Small sizes.** For avatars in a list, `antenna={false}` drops the antenna's stem and its light, keeping the knob on top, so the head itself fills more of the box (the square, circle and hexagon grow; the wide rectangle is already as big as its width allows).
- **Reduced motion.** With `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, or `paused`, the still pose of the state is drawn instead of the animation.
- **Accessible by default.** The canvas has `role="img"` and an `aria-label` naming the state ("Robot, thinking"); pass your own `aria-label` to override it.
- **Cheap to run many.** Every head on the page shares one animation loop, which sleeps while the tab is hidden, and heads of the same shape and size share their baked textures.

## How it is drawn

The head is real geometry: a shell with a rolled edge — its outline a convex polygon of corner centres grown by a corner radius, so one builder makes every shape — lathed knob ears and an antenna collar, built once as quad meshes. Each frame it is turned with the pose and projected, back faces are culled, and every quad is lit by a small studio model: a key light, a fill, a sky dome, a softbox and the key's window caught as clear-coat reflections with Fresnel, a cool back light rimming the silhouette, and a filmic tone curve.

The flat front and back are plates drawn in their own plane with baked relief: the lip rolling into the screen hole, the rubber gasket, the shadow the lip casts onto the glass, screws, and vents on the back. The glass sits a little behind the bezel, so it slides against it as the head turns. The LED matrix covers the whole screen, the face centred on it; the LEDs are drawn crisp, then bloomed from a one-pixel-per-LED image scaled up smooth. The antenna is a damped spring that whips when the head hops, lands or tilts, topped with a frosted bulb lit from inside.

## Development

The repo is a pnpm workspace: the library at the root, the playground in `site/` — a React app on [Vite](https://vite.dev) served by a [Cloudflare Worker](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/). The playground runs on the library's source, so edits hot-reload there.

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm run dev       # the playground
pnpm run build     # the library, to dist/
pnpm run typecheck
pnpm run deploy    # build and deploy the playground Worker
```

```
src/            the library
  RobotHead.tsx   the component
  tv/             the TV head: geometry, lighting, faces, motion, renderer
site/           the playground (Vite + Cloudflare Worker)
```

## License

[MIT](LICENSE) © [Fayaz Ahmed](https://x.com/fayazara)

The playground is set in [Open Runde](https://github.com/lauridskern/open-runde) by Laurids Kern, under the SIL Open Font License 1.1 (`site/public/fonts/OFL.txt`). The font is not part of the npm package.

extra.description: An agent skill that builds award-caliber websites from one line
extra.source_text:
An agent skill that builds award-caliber websites from one line
# /awwwards **An agent skill that builds award-caliber websites from one line.**

[Demo](#demo) · [Install](#install) · [Usage](#usage) · [How it works](#how-it-works) · [Limits](#limits)
``` > make me a portfolio, my name is Julio ``` That's the whole brief. The agent works as creative director, designer and creative developer in one, then hands back a site it has already checked in a real browser. ## Quick start ```bash npx skills add wheresryan22/anatomy -g # optional: interactive isometric explainer figures npx skills add juliobsz/skills -g ``` Open a **new** agent session, then type `/awwwards` or just ask for a website. ## Demo [![Watch the demo on YouTube](https://img.youtube.com/vi/BEcQoDs16IE/maxresdefault.jpg)](https://youtu.be/BEcQoDs16IE) Click on the thumbnail to watch the demo on YouTube ## Install Install with the [skills CLI](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills). It runs through `npx`, so there's nothing to install first, and it detects your agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Copilot and more) and lets you pick. ```bash npx skills add juliobsz/skills -g ``` | Command | Result | |---|---| | `npx skills add juliobsz/skills -g -a claude-code` | Claude Code only (use `codex`, `cursor`… for others) | | `npx skills add juliobsz/skills` | This project only, instead of your user folder | | `npx skills add juliobsz/skills -g --copy` | Copy the files instead of linking them | | `npx skills update -g` | Update to the latest version | | `npx skills remove awwwards -g` | Uninstall | The CLI collects anonymous usage data. Set `DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1` or `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` to turn it off.
Claude Code plugin If you prefer Claude Code's plugin system, which updates the skill for you: ``` /plugin install awwwards --marketplace juliobsz/skills ``` On Claude Code before 2.1.275, run `/plugin marketplace add juliobsz/skills` and then `/plugin install awwwards@juliobsz`. The skill then runs as `/awwwards:awwwards`. Use the plugin or the skills CLI, not both, or the skill shows up twice.
Manual install Copy the `awwwards/` folder into your agent's skills directory, for example `~/.claude/skills/awwwards`. Any agent that reads `SKILL.md` skills can use it.
### Works with /anatomy [/anatomy](https://github.com/wheresryan22/anatomy) by wheresryan22 is an open-source skill for detailed, interactive isometric figures that explain an idea as a real physical object. Install it next to `/awwwards` and the site can get one "how it works" section built as a real explainer figure, styled to the site's palette and grid. ```bash npx skills add wheresryan22/anatomy -g ``` It's optional. Without it, `/awwwards` builds that section another way, and tells you at the end when a figure would have helped. ### Requirements - **Node 22.20+** for the skills CLI. The helper scripts need Node 20+. - **Playwright** in the site's project for screenshots and the OG image, and **axe-core** for the accessibility pass. The skill installs both as dev dependencies when it needs them, and uses a Chromium you already have when it can. - **A model that can read images**, so the QA loop can look at its own screenshots. - **A Vercel, Netlify or Cloudflare account** only if you want it to deploy.
Troubleshooting - **`/awwwards` isn't found.** Start a new session; agents read their skills folder at startup. Then run `npx skills list -g` to see where it was installed. - **It shows up twice.** You installed it two ways (for example the skills CLI and the plugin). Remove one with `npx skills remove awwwards -g` or `/plugin uninstall awwwards@juliobsz`. - **Installed into the wrong agent.** Name the target with `-a`, for example `-a codex`. - **Screenshots fail with "Playwright not found".** Run `npm i -D playwright` in the site's project. If it reports no Chromium, run `npx playwright install chromium` once.
## Why Ask an agent for "a portfolio" and you get the same site everyone gets: purple gradient, three cards, "elevate your brand". This skill replaces that default with a process. - **A concept that belongs to you.** Three ideas from different territories (your name, your craft, your place), scored on originality and fit. - **A real design system.** Palette by role, curated free fonts, grid and motion language, written to `DESIGN.md` and tested against a "genericness check". - **Motion with intent.** GSAP, Lenis and WebGL (OGL) where they earn their place, with one signature moment and everything else quiet. - **Real copy.** No lorem ipsum, fake awards or invented metrics. Anything made up is marked as a placeholder and listed at the end. - **Verified, not assumed.** A production build, a crawling audit and real-browser screenshots on desktop, mobile and reduced motion, scored against a rubric until every category hits 8/10. Its quality bar is the work that wins [Awwwards](https://www.awwwards.com) Site of the Day. The site doesn't need to be submitted anywhere; it just has to be that good. ## Usage Ask in one line and let the agent decide. It writes its assumptions down instead of running a questionnaire. ``` make me a portfolio, my name is Ana a site for my architecture studio in Lisbon, we do small houses launch page for a mechanical keyboard called Kestrel, it should feel insane redesign this landing page so it could win site of the day ``` Better input gives a better site. Your real name, what you do, where you are and two or three real projects let the concept come from your story instead of a placeholder. ## How it works | Phase | What happens | |---|---| | **Brief** | Infers who it's for, the audience and the site's job. Missing facts become written assumptions | | **Concept** | Three concepts from different territories (your name, your craft's materials, your place, how you work, a formal system), scored on originality and fit. The winner becomes a one-line idea with a signature moment | | **Art direction** | Palette by role, type pairing from a curated free-font library, grid, rhythm and motion language, all written to `DESIGN.md`. Then a "genericness test" kills anything an average model would have produced | | **Build** | Semantic HTML that looks finished with motion off. Then reveals, page transitions, a loader that tracks real loading, and the signature moment | | **QA loop** | Production build, a crawling audit (SEO, metadata, accessibility, weight, placeholder copy, AI-copy tells) and real-browser screenshots on desktop, mobile, reduced motion and mid-transition. It also measures LCP and CLS on a throttled phone, runs axe and tabs through every page. The agent reads every frame, a fresh critic subagent that never saw the plan scores the site against the rubric, and the agent fixes things until every category hits 8/10 | | **Ship** | OG image, favicon, sitemap, robots, then deploy to Vercel, Netlify or Cloudflare (only after you confirm) | ### Stack - **Next.js** (App Router) by default, and for anything with app features. - **Astro** for content-only showcases where motion is the product: about 75 KB of JS against about 250 KB. - **Your stack** when you run it inside an existing project. All three use [GSAP](https://gsap.com) (every plugin is free now), [Lenis](https://lenis.dev) for smooth scroll and [OGL](https://github.com/oframe/ogl) for WebGL. The motion engine is framework-agnostic TypeScript, shipped as documented code instead of a template: it runs on one clock, reverts every effect on navigation, runs transitions in parallel with the next page loading, and keeps content visible without JavaScript or with reduced motion. ### Principles it won't break - One idea, one signature moment, everything else quiet. - Every frame works as a still poster before any motion is added. - The native cursor stays. Reduced motion gets a complete, calm site. Phones get a composed layout, not a shrunken one. - No fake awards, logos or metrics. No lorem ipsum. No em dashes or "elevate your brand" copy. - No purple gradients, glassmorphism or three-card grids unless the concept truly calls for them. ## Limits - **It takes a while.** A full run is concept, design system, build and several rounds of screenshots and fixes. Expect a long session and heavy token use, not a quick snippet. - **Results depend on the model.** It was built and tested with Claude Code and Codex. The concept and the visual QA are only as good as the model doing them. - **Content is yours to finish.** Without real projects, photos and copy, the site ships with clearly marked placeholders that you replace. - **8/10 is its own score.** The rubric keeps it honest, but you're the final judge. ## Standalone scripts The helpers in `awwwards/scripts/` work on any site, so you can use them on their own: ```bash node ~/.claude/skills/awwwards/scripts/audit.mjs https://your-site.com/ node ~/.claude/skills/awwwards/scripts/shoot.mjs https://your-site.com/ --crawl --nav ``` | Script | Does | |---|---| | `audit.mjs` | Crawl a build: SEO, a11y, weight, placeholders, AI-copy tells | | `shoot.mjs` | Screenshots of every page type: LCP/CLS on a throttled phone, FPS, overflow, tap targets, axe, keyboard focus, rest/hover pairs per pointer target, idle motion, transitions (needs Playwright; axe-core optional) | | `og.mjs` | Render the OG image from the live hero (needs Playwright) | | `font.mjs` | Self-host Fontshare / Google fonts (CSS or `next/font` output) | | `photos.mjs` | Contact sheets of free photos for marked placeholders | | `serve.mjs` | Static server for build output |

--- ## 截图 · Screenshots

--- ## 中文 **Win顺** 是 Windows 上免费开源的快速搜索启动器：连按两下 Ctrl 弹出搜索框，边打字边出结果。按文件名或拼音秒找文件，搜 Word、Excel、PDF 里的文字，打开应用和系统设置，还有剪贴板历史、对话框搜索、任务栏搜索框、插件和给 AI 用的 MCP 搜索。 它直接读 NTFS 主文件表（MFT）建索引，三百多万个文件几秒建好，增删改名实时跟上，**不用装 Everything**。不需要账号，不上传数据。界面有简体中文和英文。 ### 功能 #### 🔍 文件搜索 - **双击 Ctrl** 打开，再按一次或 `Esc` 关闭；三百多万个文件里搜一次只要几毫秒。 - **拼音和首字母**：`ndbg` → 年度报告，`baog` → 报告；多音字按常用读音。打错了同音字（年度报高）找不到时，自动按读音再找一遍。 - **搜整台电脑**：所有本地磁盘，U 盘可选（没收录的 U 盘插着时，列表末尾会提示你顺手搜一下它）；**NAS、内网共享文件夹（SMB）** 也能加进来一起搜，服务器关机时收录过的照样能搜到。 - **排序懂你**：自己的文件在前，系统目录、`node_modules` 在后，名字完全一样的最前。每行显示修改日期，`Ctrl+S` 在最匹配、最新、最早之间切换。不输入时列出最近打开或最近修改的文件。 - **数字键直达**：结果的图标上标着序号，`Ctrl+1`～`Ctrl+9` 打开第几行（也可改成 `Alt`）。 - **按类型找**：选中 **文件** 后，下面一排是文件夹、文档、图片、视频、压缩包等类型，`Tab` 依次切换；点 `+` 或在设置里自己加类型。 - **拖出去就能用**：结果直接拖进微信、邮件、资源管理器。 - **实时更新**：读 USN 变更日志，改名、新建、删除马上搜得到；拔 U 盘不会提示“设备正在使用”。 | 搜索语法 | 含义 | |---|---| | `报告 2024` | 每个词都要有（空格分隔，顺序不限）；也可以在所在文件夹的名字里 | | `ndbg`、`niandubaogao` | 拼音全拼、首字母，可以混用 | | `"年度 报告"` | 引号内作为整体 | | `!草稿`、`!node_modules\` | 排除文件名、排除文件夹 | | `*.pdf`、`报告?.docx` | 通配符 | | `ext:pdf,docx` | 只要这些扩展名 | | `项目\readme` | 在名字含“项目”的文件夹下 | | `tools/out/`、`D:\My Files\` | 路径直达：回车进去，列出里面的内容 | #### 📄 文件内容全文搜索 - 切到 **内容** 范围，搜文件里的文字，结果显示命中的那一行。 - **能搜的文件**： - 纯文本：txt、md、log、csv、json、代码等； - 文档：**Word、Excel、PowerPoint、PDF、WPS**，结果里显示第几页、第几张幻灯片或哪个表的第几行。 - **怎么找**：可以写多个词、用引号找整个短语，结果按相关度排。 - **编码和速度**：自动识别 UTF-8、UTF-16、GBK 编码；有内容索引，几十万个文件也很快。超过大小上限的、系统目录里的、类型没列出的文件默认不搜，搜完会告诉你各有几个，点一下就临时把它们也搜了。 - **安全**：文档由一个权限受限的独立进程读取。 #### 🚀 应用和系统设置 - **应用**：开始菜单里的所有应用都能搜，含 Microsoft Store 应用。名称、拼音、首字母（`vsc`）、程序名（`winword`）都行；`Ctrl+Shift+Enter` 以管理员身份运行。 - **系统设置**：约 1200 个 Windows 设置页和控制面板项。`shipeiqi`、“网卡”、`ncpa.cpl` 都能打开网络连接；另外补了组策略、磁盘管理、hosts、AppData 等开始菜单里没有的。 #### 🌐 网页搜索 · ⭐ 收藏夹 · 🧩 插件 - **网页搜索**：`baidu 天气`、`zhihu 显卡`、`jingdong 键盘`，关键词加空格就在那个网站上搜。 - 自带百度、必应、B 站、知乎、微博、抖音、小红书、淘宝、京东、翻译。 - 可以用 `%s` 网址添加自己的网站，图标、列表都能导入导出。 - **收藏夹**： - 右键“加入收藏夹”，不打字时排在最前； - 起个关键词，一打就开； - 收藏的文件夹按 `Tab` 进去接着搜。 - **插件**： - 随包的小工具：`= 1+2*3` 计算器、`12 inch to cm` 单位换算、`#ff8800` 颜色，还有时间戳、UUID、Base64、哈希； - `kill` 结束进程，`bm` 搜浏览器书签，`tr` 翻译； - 自己写插件：零代码的 `plugin.json`、任意语言的脚本或常驻进程都行，附 Python / PowerShell / C++ SDK； - 插件以普通权限、限内存运行。见 [docs/plugins.md](docs/plugins.md)。 #### 📂 “打开”“另存为”对话框 - **对话框旁的搜索框**：输入文件夹或文件名（拼音也行），回车，对话框直接转过去；网页上传文件、WPS 的对话框也认。 - **`Ctrl+G`**：转到资源管理器、Total Commander 或 Directory Opus 正在显示的文件夹，和 Listary 的同名快捷键一样。 - **不输入时**：列出打开着的文件夹、刚复制的路径、收藏和最近用过的文件夹。 - **自动转过去**：可以设成对话框一出现就转到文件管理器的文件夹，或者先停在上次的位置，从文件管理器切回来时再转。 #### 📋 剪贴板历史（代替 Win+V） - **记什么**：复制过的文字、图片、文件都记下来。 - **怎么打开**：`Win+V` 或自设的快捷键；开在输入光标旁，不抢焦点。 - **怎么粘贴**：双击或 `Enter` 粘贴，`Shift+Enter` 粘贴为纯文本，`Alt+1`～`9` 直接粘贴第几条（序号标在图标上）。 - **能搜**：拼音搜索，`@wx` 只看微信里复制的；**图片里的字也能搜**（Windows 自带的文字识别 OCR，在本机，不联网）。 - **预览**：全文、大图、颜色值的 HEX / RGB / HSL。 - **拖出图片**：按住一张图片拖到文件夹里，就存成 PNG 文件。 - **整理**：固定、分组、多选按顺序合并粘贴，钉住后可以一条接一条地往表格里填。 - **隐私**：密码管理器复制的密码不记录，历史只存在本机。 #### 🔎 任务栏搜索框（代替 Windows 搜索） - 在 Windows 11 任务栏上放 Win顺 自己的搜索框（Windows 10 是固定一个按钮），结果从任务栏上方滑出。 - 可以像 Windows 自带的搜索框一样放在开始按钮右边，图标往右让出位置（设置里打开，默认关）。 - 可以接管 `Win+S`，开始菜单里打字也用 Win顺 搜。 #### 🤖 AI 助手（MCP） - **能做什么**：Win顺 是一个 MCP 服务器，AI 能用它搜文件名、文件内容和最近修改的文件。 - **怎么连**：Claude Desktop、Claude Code、Cursor、VS Code 在设置里一键连接。 - **安全**： - 默认只读，只看得到 AI 客户端自己有权限看的文件； - 可以设不让 AI 看到的文件夹； - 每次调用都有记录。 #### 🎨 外观和设置 - **外观**：浅色、深色跟随系统，Windows 11 云母（Mica）效果和圆角；图标在 150% 缩放下也清晰。 - **设置**：可以搜索（`Ctrl+F`，`kjj` 找到“快捷键”），改了立即生效。 - **更新**：有新版本时在托盘提醒，Win顺 不会自己下载、替换程序文件。 | 按键 | 作用 | |---|---| | 双击 `Ctrl` | 打开 / 关闭搜索框（可另设组合键，如 `Alt+Space`） | | `Enter` / `Ctrl+Enter` / `Ctrl+Shift+Enter` | 打开 / 打开所在文件夹 / 以管理员身份运行 | | `Ctrl+C` / `Ctrl+Shift+C` | 复制文件 / 复制路径 | | `Ctrl+1`～`Ctrl+9` | 打开第几行（图标上的数字） | | `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | 切换范围：全部 / 文件 / 内容；在 **文件** 里 `Tab` 切换类型 | | `Ctrl+S` | 最匹配 → 最新在前 → 最早在前 | | `Ctrl+G`（对话框里） | 转到文件管理器正在显示的文件夹 | | `Win+V` / `Win+S`（设置里打开后） | 剪贴板历史 / 任务栏上方的搜索框 | ### 下载安装 1. 到 [Releases 页面](https://github.com/LingCore/WinShun/releases/latest) 下载 `WinShun-版本号-x64-setup.exe`，双击安装。Windows 提示“已保护你的电脑”时，点 **更多信息 → 仍要运行**（还没有代码签名证书）。 2. 装完托盘里出现 Win顺 的图标，索引几秒就建好。连按两下 Ctrl 开始搜索。 3. 升级时运行新的安装程序，设置和索引都保留。卸载在 Windows 的“设置 → 应用”里。 不想安装的话，下载 `WinShun-版本号-x64-portable.zip`，解压到任意文件夹，运行里面的 `WinShun.exe` 就行。设置和索引和安装版放在同一个地方（`%APPDATA%\WinShun`、`%LOCALAPPDATA%\WinShun`），不在解压的文件夹里；升级时用新版的文件夹换掉旧的。 系统要求：Windows 10 或 11，64 位。 ### 为什么需要管理员权限 - **为什么要**：读 NTFS 主文件表（MFT）和 USN 变更日志，才能几秒建好索引、实时跟上改动。开机自启用的是最高权限的计划任务，所以开机不弹 UAC。 - **打开的东西仍是普通权限**：从 Win顺 打开的文件和应用都以普通权限运行，只有 `Ctrl+Shift+Enter` 才以管理员身份运行。 ### 常见问题 **和 Everything、Listary 有什么区别？** Win顺 自己建索引，不用装 Everything。文件名、拼音、应用和文件内容在一个框里搜，针对中文做了优化。对话框里有和 Listary 一样的 `Ctrl+G` 和搜索框，但不嵌进资源管理器窗口。 **双击 Ctrl 和别的软件冲突？** Listary、PowerToys 的“查找鼠标”默认也用双击 Ctrl，关掉其中一边就行。也可以在 Win顺 里改用别的组合键。游戏全屏、藏起鼠标时，Win顺 默认不响应双击 Ctrl。 **AutoHotkey 改的键在 Win顺 里不起作用？** Win顺 以管理员身份运行，Windows 不让普通权限的程序拦截发给它的按键。用 AutoHotkey 的 UI Access 模式，或以管理员身份运行脚本。 **占多少内存？索引能不放 C 盘吗？** - **内存**：每 100 万个文件约 30 MB，用着的时候整个程序一般 120～140 MB；不用它一分钟后，任务管理器里降到十几 MB。 - **索引位置**：在设置 → 高级 → 索引位置里，可以移到其他内置硬盘。 **收费吗？会上传数据吗？** 完全免费，MIT 开源。只在两种时候联网：到 GitHub 检查新版本（可以关掉），第一次显示某个网页搜索时取一次那个网站的图标。索引和历史只存在本机（`%LOCALAPPDATA%\WinShun`）。 ### 反馈 遇到问题或有建议，欢迎在 [Issues](https://github.com/LingCore/WinShun/issues) 里提出。 ### 从源码编译 需要 Visual Studio 2022（“使用 C++ 的桌面开发”）、Qt 6.8 或更新版本（推荐 6.12，MSVC 2022 64 位套件）、CMake 3.25+ 和 Ninja。 ```powershell ./scripts/build.ps1 # 编译 + 运行单元测试 ./scripts/build.ps1 -QtDir C:\Qt\6.12.0\msvc2022_64 # 指定 Qt（默认用 QTDIR 或 C:\Qt 下最新的版本） ./scripts/build.ps1 -Deploy # 生成可分发的文件夹 dist\WinShun ./scripts/release.ps1 # 打包安装程序和 SHA256SUMS.txt（需要 Inno Setup 6.5+）；加 -Publish 发布到 GitHub ``` 也可以用 Qt Creator 或 VS Code（CMake Tools）打开，预设见 `CMakePresets.json`。源码结构和设计见 [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md)，踩过的坑见 [docs/pitfalls.md](docs/pitfalls.md)。 --- ## English **WinShun** (Win顺, "Windows made smooth") is a free, open-source search launcher for Windows. Press Ctrl twice and a search bar pops up, with results as you type: - find files and folders by name or by pinyin; - search the text inside Word, Excel and PDF files; - launch apps and open Windows settings. It also brings a clipboard history, a search bar for file dialogs, a taskbar search box, plugins and an MCP server for AI assistants. It reads the NTFS master file table (MFT) directly, indexing three million files in a few seconds and following every change live: **no Everything install needed**. It needs no account and uploads nothing. The interface comes in English and Simplified Chinese. Screenshots: [above](#screenshots). ### Features
